objects.taxonomy_description: Stringed instrument with solid or semi-hollow body (no sound hole required). Body shape varies: Stratocaster (double-cutaway, contoured edges), Les Paul (single-cutaway, carved top), Telecaster (single-cutaway, slab body). Body is wood (alder, mahogany, maple) with glossy polyester or nitrocellulose finish in solid colors, sunburst, or natural wood grain. Neck is maple or mahogany with fretted fingerboard (rosewood or maple, 21-24 frets). Pickups (magnetic, 1-3) mounted on body. Control knobs (volume, tone) and pickup selector switch. Bridge is fixed or tremolo. Headstock has 6 tuning pegs. Cable jack on body edge.

objects.taxonomy_description: Equine mammal measuring 140-170 cm at withers with athletic build. Coat uniform brownish-orange to light chestnut coloration with no black points. Mane and tail same color as body or lighter (flaxen). Head elongated with large expressive eyes and mobile ears. Neck arched and muscular. Body deep-chested with strong back. Legs long and slender with single hoof per foot. Tail long with flowing hair. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, sparse body hair, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. Color variant of horse distinguished by reddish-brown coat.

objects.taxonomy_description: An inanimate manufactured object designed for play, distinguished from living organisms by its artificial construction and lack of biological features.

diagnostic_checkpoints.Material_Composition: The object exhibits synthetic textures such as molded plastic, plush fabric, or painted surfaces rather than organic skin, fur, or scales.
diagnostic_checkpoints.Structural_Anatomy: The form lacks biologically accurate anatomical structures such as joints, musculature, or functional sensory organs like eyes with pupils.
diagnostic_checkpoints.Surface_Finish: Visible seams, mold lines, or uniform artificial coloring indicate industrial manufacturing processes instead of natural growth patterns.
diagnostic_checkpoints.Biological_Viability: The object shows no signs of life, such as respiration, movement, or interaction with the environment typical of living creatures.
